propositions: The transition command has two semantically distinct --force flags (one for start-work gate, one for close gate) that do not align with claim command's --force spelling, causing operator confusion and incorrect documentation.

Collapsing transition's two force flags into a single --force[=<reason>] whose meaning depends on target status (start-work or close gate bypass) eliminates the collision and unifies CLI spelling across commands.

The parser must explicitly reject the retired --force-close flag with a CommandError naming --force rather than silently skipping it, to prevent stale callers from unknowingly losing their gate bypass.
Explicit --force=<reason> on open->in_progress transition now becomes the audit note (falling back to --reason), preserving the semantics of existing --force --reason=X invocations.
Bare --force on a close gate bypass records (no reason given) as the reason, achieving parity with claim command behavior.

A concurrent change landing after the rename (scripts/dependency_audit.py) still emitted the retired flag, causing runtime CommandError, requiring post-merge defect fix and a guard test that feeds generated argv to the real parser.
